subject: SIEM evidence orchestration for private VPC deployment - onboarding playbook
messages:
From: Ops (ACME) <ops+acme@acme.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: LogTrace Support <ingest@logtrace.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIEM onboarding — minimal evidence bundle & export cadence for VPC deployment

Marissa,

Thanks for the intro. We're ready to start the SIEM ingestion validation for our Redwood private deployment inside the ACME VPC. A few goals and asks from our side to make the acceptance runbook executable: 

- Minimal evidence bundle: 30 minutes of representative logs (app + inference runtime), a sample trace span export for a failed request, and one anonymized user payload.
- Preferred transport: HTTPS to LogTrace HEC endpoint (ingest.logtrace.acme:443) with mTLS.
- Token/credential rotation: we rotate HEC tokens nightly; can Redwood accept ephemeral tokens (10m TTL) or do you prefer long-lived certs?
- Metadata: require RFC3339 timestamps, instance_id, model_variant, and request_id on each event.
- Retention & sampling: we'll request a 72hr hot window and 30d cold archive for the proof stage.

I'm attaching an example bundle and a short ingest spec to show formats (acme-sample-logs-20260301.json, siem-ingest-spec.xlsx). Can your team confirm: 1) the network egress pattern (single IP vs range); 2) the expected acceptance test checklist and timing; 3) any additional evidence pieces you need for SOC/PCI artifacts?

Proposed timeline: acceptance test window week of Mar 15; handover docs by Mar 10.

Thanks,
David Brown
ACME — Platform Operations
ops+acme@acme.com

Attachments: acme-sample-logs-20260301.json (json), siem-ingest-spec.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ops (ACME) <ops+acme@acme.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIEM onboarding — minimal evidence bundle & export cadence for VPC deployment

David — thanks, this is very clear. Looping in Kim and Jonas to confirm the runbook details. High level answers and proposed next steps below:

- Egress: we prefer a short list of CIDR ranges (for firewall allowlisting) rather than a single ephemeral IP. We'll provide the ranges for both the forwarder and the private egress gateway.
- Credentials: we support both mTLS (preferred for Private) and short-lived HEC tokens. For the acceptance test let's use mTLS certs; we'll show token rotation support during the canary.
- Evidence checklist (draft):
  1) Sample logs (30m) + representative trace spans (single trace per error scenario)
  2) Forwarder config used (vpc-forwarder-config.yaml)
  3) Network egress ranges + expected SNI/hostnames
  4) Retention policy summary + proof of delivery (HEC success receipts)
  5) Hash/signed manifest for bundle integrity (example-evidence-bundle.tar.gz)

Action items: 
- Kim: can you confirm the exact CIDR ranges and cert thumbprint format we will publish?
- Jonas: please draft the acceptance test steps (canary, sampling, failure injection) and link to the test runbook in Drive.
- David: if you can provide one failing request trace and the app logs for the same window that will accelerate validation.

I'll prepare the playbook and a short runbook link by EOD tomorrow.

— Marissa
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDefgh-Observability/preview
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: david.brown@acme.com, LogTrace Support <ingest@logtrace.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIEM onboarding — CIDR, cert format, and forwarder config

Marissa / team — quick technical checklist and clarifying questions so the acceptance playbook is unambiguous:

Checklist (deliverables we will verify during acceptance):
- Forwarder TLS: mTLS with leaf cert issued by ACME PKI; we need PEM chain and cert thumbprint (SHA256) to validate during handshake.
- CIDR allowlist: please allow these ranges for outbound egress from the VPC forwarder: 52.34.120.0/22, 34.210.0.0/18 (these are Redwood egress endpoints). We'll provide final dataplane range for the forwarder gateway.
- Payload schema: each event must include: timestamp (RFC3339), request_id, model_variant, latency_ms, instance_id, level, message. If trace spans are exported separately, include parent_id and span_id.
- HEC receipts: acceptance requires HTTP 202 from LogTrace for sample batches and an HEC ACK header.
- Evidence bundle integrity: SHA256 manifest for the tarball (example-evidence-bundle.tar.gz).

Questions: 
1) For traces: do you have an existing OTel collector we should point to, or do you want Redwood to export OTel JSON directly to LogTrace?
2) Sampling: can you identify which endpoints should be 100% sampled for the test (e.g., inference/stream, inference/generate)?

Attached a starter forwarder config we use in on-prem proofs (vpc-forwarder-config.yaml). Also: for SOC related artifacts, we will need a signed attestation of retention policy from your compliance team during the final handoff.

— Kim
Director, Observability Integrations, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Attachments: vpc-forwarder-config.yaml (text)
From: David Brown <david.brown@acme.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: LogTrace Support <ingest@logtrace.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIEM onboarding — answers on traces and sampling

Kim / Marissa — quick answers: 

- OTel: ACME runs a central OTel collector in the VPC (collector.acme.internal). We'd prefer Redwood to POST OTel JSON to that collector during the acceptance test; LogTrace will pull from the collector using the HEC connector afterwards.
- Sampling: we'll set 100% sampling for the inference/generate endpoint and 10% for streaming endpoints for the acceptance window.
- Certs: we'll provision a short-lived client cert for the mTLS handshake (valid 7 days) and provide PEM + thumbprint by Mar 9.
- SOC artifact: compliance team can produce a signed retention attestation; I'll open a ticket and share the PDF to the drive link.

Attached a trimmed sample of the failing request trace and logs for the same timeframe (acme-sample-logs-20260301.json).

Thanks — launching cert request now.

— David
Platform Ops — ACME Financial
ops+acme@acme.com

Attachments: acme-sample-logs-20260301.json (json)
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: David Brown <david.brown@acme.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIEM onboarding — acceptance window & canary plan

David — great, thanks for the quick turnaround and the sample bundle. Finalizing the acceptance playbook now; summary and next milestones below:

- Publish: We'll drop the draft playbook in the Drive folder by EOD (link above). It will include the canary steps, failure-injection checklist, and the exact HEC receipt assertions we will validate.
- Canary test: propose Mar 16 09:00–11:00 PT for a 2-hour canary window with 100% sampling on inference/generate. Redwood will perform a synthetic failure injection at +45m to validate trace capture.
- Evidence artifacts: please upload the signed retention attestation and the PEM/thumbprint to the same Drive folder by Mar 10. We'll require HEC receipts and the SHA256 manifest as part of the pass criteria.
- Post-acceptance: if canary passes we'll schedule a single-day production cutover (low traffic) to verify long-run retention and ingestion.

If anyone on the Redwood side sees outstanding gaps please flag them; otherwise we'll treat the runbook as approved pending the items above.

— Marissa
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
